chunks: And whatever is in it from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, I have narrated it from my father, and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Nu'man.

key_terms.السَّعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key link in the chain of transmission
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith literature
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: May Allah be pleased with them, a phrase of approval used for the narrators

ai.seo_question: How is the chain of narration verified for Hadith from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Nu'man?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous chain-of-transmission (isnad) methodology central to Shia hadith scholarship, specifically within Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. By explicitly linking the narrator to his father and then to prominent figures like Sa'd ibn Abdullah, it underscores the reliability and continuity of the scholarly lineage (thiqa) essential for validating legal rulings.
